description: Shared semantic corpus for the Hebrew-only rule that both runtimes apply to model copy. TypeScript runs it through the callback validator's predicate, Python through is_hebrew_only_copy. The rule judges letters only: digits, punctuation, Hebrew points and whitespace are not letters here, and the per-version limits that forbid digits in narrative copy live elsewhere.

cases.text: הצוות מדווח על עומס מתמשך בשבועות האחרונים.
cases.note: The ordinary case: every letter is Hebrew.
Digits are not letters. Contracts that forbid numbers in narrative copy enforce that separately.

cases.text: "שיחה קצרה" עוזרת לצוות; כך עולה מן התשובות.
cases.note: Quotes, semicolons and periods are not letters.
Hebrew points are combining marks, not letters.
U+FB2A is the precomposed shin a model may emit instead of the base letter plus its point. It reads as Hebrew, so it counts as Hebrew.
The one script the old TypeScript rule refused.
A whole sentence in Cyrillic used to pass Core's callback validation as long as one Hebrew letter stood somewhere in it.
The Arabic waw a provider sent twice on 2026-07-30. The generation pipeline repairs this confusable before validating; a payload that reaches the callback with it unrepaired is refused.
Any script other than Hebrew, not a named list of refused ones.
At least one Hebrew letter is required, and digits are not letters.
Empty copy is not Hebrew copy.
